review_candidates.title: Data Center Operations Implementation Manager
review_candidates.description: Role Overview We are seeking a Data Center Operations Implementation Manager to own the end-to-end Day 0 to Day 2 transition of Nscale's data centres — spanning construction, fit-out, and live, steady-state local operations — across an assigned region and set of sites. Rather than owning construction execution itself, you'll be the connective tissue between Construction, Network Engineering, Compute/Infrastructure Deployment, and local Operations teams — driving a structured, well-documented transition so every site goes live on schedule and ready to support production workloads. This is an individual-contributor role built on strong stakeholder management, cross-functional influence, and travel to sites during critical transition windows. What You'll Do Day 0 to Day 2 Transition Leadership Own the end-to-end Day 0 to Day 2 transition process for each data centre site within your assigned region — spanning construction, fit-out, and steady-state operations. Define and maintain a standardized transition framework and readiness checklist applied consistently across your assigned sites. Track and drive closure of cross-team action items, dependencies, and blockers standing between construction handover and operational go-live. Identify and escalate risks to go-live timelines, and drive resolution across the relevant stakeholder groups. Stakeholder & Cross-Functional Coordination Track progress and status across Construction, Network Engineering, Compute/Infrastructure Deployment, Facility Engineering, SDM, and local site Operations teams throughout the transition window. Partner with Construction teams to track handover status, outstanding items, and site readiness milestones. Track Network Engineering's buildout, testing, and cutover activities required for a site to go live. Track hardware intake, rack-and-stack, and deployment scheduling with Compute/Infrastructure Deployment teams to stay aligned with the transition timeline. Coordinate with Facility Engineering on site systems and infrastructure readiness ahead of transition. Engage with the Service Delivery Management (SDM) team to ensure alignment with customer needs, SLAs, security, and facility performance. Take part in regular cross-functional syncs and stakeholder reviews to stay current on transition status. Contribute to a shared sense of ownership and accountability across stakeholder teams, even without formal authority over them. Local Day Two Operations Readiness Partner with local Operations leads to confirm staffing, training, tooling, and support processes are in place before a site transitions to Day 2 ownership. Create and validate standard operating procedures (SOPs) and operational processes required for local Operations teams to run the site post-handover. Create the operational site tool bill of materials (BOM) required for local Operations teams to maintain the site post-handover. Verify the spare parts bill of materials (BOM) is complete and in place ahead of Day 2 handover. Facilitate structured knowledge transfer and handover documentation from Construction, Network, and Compute teams to local Operations teams. Confirm monitoring, ticketing, and ITSM processes are validated and operating before a site is handed to local Operations. Act as an escalation point for local Operations teams during the early post-handover period to smooth the transition. Reliability, Safety & Compliance Define and enforce Day 2 readiness criteria that a site must meet before transitioning to local Operations ownership. Facilitate root-cause analysis for transition delays or gaps surfaced during handover, and drive remediation across teams. Ensure health, safety, and environmental requirements are validated and documented as part of readiness sign-off. Support certification and audit readiness (ISO 27001, ISO 22237, SOC 2, Cyber Essentials Plus, ISO 22301) ahead of go-live. Vendor & Supplier Coordination Coordinate with construction contractors and colocation providers as needed to close out remaining items affecting the transition timeline. Track vendor commitments and SLAs relevant to the transition window, and escalate delays that put go-live at risk. Coordinate with the Supply Chain team to align hardware intake and staging with the transition schedule. Monitoring, Reporting & Analytics Track KPIs and KRIs for the Day 0 to Day 2 transition process (time to transition, readiness checklist completion rate, post-handover incident rate, etc.). Build and maintain dashboards that track transition status across your assigned site pipeline for all stakeholder teams. Produce regular reports for senior leadership on transition status, risks, and blockers. Use data-driven insights to identify systemic bottlenecks in the Day 0 to Day 2 process and drive continuous improvement. About You Experience & Background 3-8 years of experience in data centre operations, program/project management, or infrastructure deployment at scale. Proven track record coordinating the transition of new sites into live operations across construction, network, compute, and operations functions. Experience operating in a matrixed environment, influencing outcomes without direct authority over every stakeholder team. Demonstrated success managing multiple concurrent site transitions in a high-growth, fast-paced environment. Background in hyperscale, cloud, or HPC data centre environments (preferred). Technical Knowledge & Expertise Working knowledge of data centre power, cooling, networking, and compute infrastructure, sufficient to coordinate effectively across specialist teams. review_candidates.description: Overview Nakupuna Solutions seeks an Executive Assistant to support the U.S. Department of State’s Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy (GHSD). GHSD leads and coordinates the Department’s work to strengthen global health security and prevent, detect, and respond to infectious diseases, including HIV/AIDS. The Bureau leads U.S. diplomatic engagement, leverages and helps coordinate U.S. foreign assistance, and promotes international cooperation at the national, regional, and multilateral levels to better protect the United States and the world from health threats. GHSD elevates and integrates global health security as a core component of U.S. national security and foreign policy. The Executive Assistant will support GHSD offices and teams as they advance U.S. global health priorities, including implementation of the America First Global Health Strategy (AFGHS). The position may be assigned to support Health Programs, Health Diplomacy, Outbreak Detection and Response, Program Transition and Supply Chain, Program Planning and Evaluation, the Foreign Assistance Hub, the CGFS Budget Team, or another designated GHSD-supported office or team. The Executive Assistant will provide comprehensive administrative and operational support to office leadership and staff, helping ensure schedules, meetings, travel, correspondence, briefing materials, visitor access, and other office requirements are managed efficiently and professionally. The position requires exceptional organization, discretion, responsiveness, and attention to detail, as well as the ability to manage multiple competing priorities and work effectively with senior Department officials, interagency partners, international stakeholders, and other external partners. Responsibilities The following reflects management’s definition of essential functions for this job but does not restrict the tasks that may be assigned. Management may assign additional duties and responsibilities to this job at any time due to reasonable accommodation or other reasons. Scheduling and Calendar Management: Manage and maintain office leadership calendars, including meetings, appointments, events, and other commitments. Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to schedule engagements, resolve scheduling conflicts, and ensure leadership has appropriate time and information to meet priority requirements. Adjust schedules and appointments as requirements change and maintain awareness of competing priorities, deadlines, and office commitments. Meeting and Event Coordination: Coordinate meetings, briefings, conferences, and events, including scheduling participants, reserving meeting space, arranging virtual participation, and supporting associated logistics. Prepare, print, organize, and distribute briefing materials, agendas, read-ahead packages, and other meeting materials. Take and prepare meeting notes, summaries, or action items for international, interagency, internal, or public meetings as required. Travel Arrangements and Support: Coordinate domestic and international travel for office leadership and staff, including transportation, lodging, itineraries, and other required arrangements. Support passport and visa processing and other international travel documentation requirements. Prepare and process travel authorizations, itineraries, vouchers, and related documentation in accordance with Department of State policies and procedures, including use of the E2 travel system or other designated Department travel-management systems. Building Access and Visitor Support: Coordinate building access and escort staff, visitors, and external stakeholders into secure Department of State facilities as required. Ensure visitor access and escort activities are conducted in accordance with applicable Department security requirements and procedures. Phone and Guest Reception: Receive and appropriately route telephone calls, inquiries, visitors, and requests for information. Greet visitors and stakeholders professionally and ensure they are connected with the appropriate office personnel. Correspondence and Briefing Support: Assist with the preparation, proofreading, formatting, routing, and distribution of correspondence, memoranda, briefing papers, reports, and other office products. Coordinate large volumes of administrative and executive-level correspondence and help ensure materials are accurate, complete, appropriately formatted, and submitted within established deadlines. Records and Communications Management: Ensure official communications and administrative records are appropriately received, routed, maintained, and handled in accordance with Department of State records-management requirements and office procedures. Maintain organized electronic and paper files, contact lists, distribution lists, administrative trackers, and other office records. Administrative and HR Support: Serve as an administrative liaison for routine personnel and HR-related matters, including performance-management reminders, leave-related procedures, awards processes, onboarding requirements, and other administrative actions. Coordinate equipment, system, workspace, and security-access requirements for new and existing personnel as appropriate. Facilities and Information Technology Coordination: Coordinate with appropriate support personnel on facilities requirements, GSO work orders, IT maintenance, computer issues, telecommunications, and other office-support needs. Office Operations: Monitor office supplies and administrative resources and coordinate procurement or replenishment as needed to maintain efficient office operations. Track administrative actions, deadlines, and outstanding requirements and follow up with responsible personnel to facilitate timely completion. Perform other duties as assigned. Qualifications Skills/Qualifications: The ideal candidate will be a highly organized, self-motivated, and service-oriented administrative professional with demonstrated experience supporting senior leaders and managing complex administrative requirements in a fast-paced professional environment. Demonstrated experience providing executive, administrative, or office support to senior leaders or senior-level professionals. Strong experience managing complex calendars, scheduling competing priorities, coordinating meetings, and supporting high-level engagements. Demonstrated experience coordinating domestic and international travel, including complex travel logistics, itineraries, lodging, transportation, passport and visa requirements, and travel vouchers. Experience using the Department of State E2 travel system desired. Excellent organizational, time-management, and multitasking skills, with the ability to manage competing requirements and rapidly changing priorities. Exceptional attention to detail and demonstrated ability to produce accurate, timely, and professional work products. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing, proofreading, editing, formatting, and routing correspondence, memoranda, briefing materials, and reports. Strong customer-service and interpersonal skills, including emotional intelligence, discretion, diplomacy, and the ability to interact professionally with senior officials, colleagues, visitors, and external stakeholders. Demonstrated ability to work effectively with senior-level contacts across the Department of State, U.S. Government interagency, international organizations, or comparable complex organizations. Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, anticipate administrative requirements, identify potential problems, and follow through on assigned actions with limited supervision. Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment and contribute to a professional, responsive, and positive workplace. Demonstrated ability to handle sensitive or confidential information appropriately and exercise discretion when supporting senior officials. Experience maintaining office files, records, administrative trackers, and other information-management systems. Proficiency with Microsoft Office 365, including Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Teams, as well as familiarity with electronic records, scheduling, collaboration, and document-management tools. Strong technological literacy and demonstrated ability to learn and effectively use Department or organizational administrative systems and procedures. Experience supporting U.S. Government, foreign affairs, international development, global health, or similarly complex organizations preferred. Education and Experience: High School Diploma or equivalent required; bachelor’s degree preferred. Minimum 6 years of progressively responsible experience in executive support, administration, office management, travel coordination, complex logistics, or a related professional support function. Six to nine years of relevant professional experience preferred. Demonstrated experience supporting senior officials or organizational leadership, including calendar management, meeting coordination, correspondence and briefing-material preparation, and travel arrangements. Experience working with senior-level U.S. Government, interagency, international, or external stakeholders preferred. Work Schedule: Position is full-time, 40 hours per week (Monday-Friday) in Washington, DC. Travel: Potential for domestic and international travel in support of Bureau requirements. Clearance Requirements: Active Secret security clearance required. Must be a US citizen.
